rows.name: In conversation: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Adam Elliot
rows.address: Brighton Library (Reading Room), 14 Wilson St, Brighton, Victoria 3186
rows.description: Don’t miss this rare opportunity to hear directly from Academy Award-winning filmmaker Adam Elliot as he discusses his work and remarkable career in conversation with Bayside Gallery Curator Joanna Bosse.

rows.name: Bayside Art Babies
rows.address: Billilla Mansion, 26 Halifax Street, Brighton, Victoria 3186
rows.description: Bayside Art Babies is aimed at supporting child development through creative arts. Designed for babies up to 18 months of age, the sessions focus on sensory stimulation and developing early cognitive skills such as visual tracking, gross motor skills and fostering bonding experiences with carers.

rows.name: Analog Art Club
rows.address: Billilla Mansion, 26 Halifax Street, Brighton, Victoria 3186
rows.description: Analog Art Club is an initiative that invites participants to slow down, switch off their screens and connect in real life, through art. This event offers a welcoming space to reflect, discuss and experience art together, making creativity social, accessible and refreshingly analog.

rows.name: Aspendale Presbyterian Church
rows.description: Aspendale Presbyterian Church is proud to be a local church. We love Jesus, love our community, love the Bible and love visitors. Our Sunday services are at 10am. We are a community of Christians who meet in Aspendale each week. We meet to hear God's truth from the Bible, encourage and support each other, and to practically live out the difference Jesus makes. As a Presbyterian church the church is lead by local elders. The Presbyterian Church originated in Scotland but welcomes all people today. rows.name: Austin 7 Club Inc Reg No A0003290N
rows.description: We are a one make Vintage Car club and provide sporting and social events, displays and runs for our members. We support the restoration and have activities for owners and supporters of all models of Austin 7 cars that were built from 1923 to 1938 by obtaining parts and technical help to keep the marque alive. Based in Cheltenham. We have 400+ members of all ages. It has always been a family club. Ladies and children are very welcome. The majority of members are in Victoria and many others from interstate with a few international members. We support all models of Austin 7's and encourage the younger members in learning the traditional skills in maintaining these older motor vehicles and their learning their history. The club runs rallies around Victoria and also join in with interstate clubs for other runs. The club has Full, Family and also Associate membership's if you don't own an Austin 7. All welcome. Our Monthly General Meeting is on the 1st Wednesday of the month except January. Meetings at 8pm The rooms open from 7:30pm for nibble & natter. The Saturday following the MGM at Noon-2:30 we open up Spare Parts & nibble & natter until 2:30 pm. And on the 3rd Wednesday 7:30-9pm for Spare parts, social chat with tea and coffee. See website www.austin7club.org.

rows.name: Bayside Bicycle Touring Club Inc
rows.description: We are a recreational cycling club based in Mordialloc, but membership is open to people from across Melbourne. Our rides are organised and conducted with most rides ideally suited to the novice and average cyclist with the emphasis of supporting and encouraging new members. We are not a competitive club and we welcome all riders. Our rides always have one thing in common: people enjoying cycling. Come and join us for healthy outdoors exercise with the companionship and security of a group. Meet new and interesting people with a common interest in cycling. Our rides program is compiled on a rolling three-month basis so there are always three months of planned rides to look forward to. rows.name: Country Women's Association (CWA) Dingley Village Branch
rows.description: Country Women's Association (CWA) of Victoria Inc is a non-party and non-sectarian organisation for all city and country women. The Dingley Village branch is just one of over 360 branches throughout the state. This group is open to women of all ages who are interested in enhancing the community in which they live. CWA encourages women of all ages to respond to the needs of the community they live in as well as becoming involved in projects that may be state wide. We care by responding to the needs of others. We participate by becoming involved in community activities. We believe in equity in the provision of our services. We provide leadership, guidance and direction. We respect ideas, potential and contribution. We provide our services in a friendly, courteous manner. We support innovation and develop skills. We meet at 10am in the Dingley Village Neighbourhood Centre, 31b Marcus Road Dingley Village on the 4th Wednesday of each month except in December. We also have a craft group that meets on the 2nd Wednesday of the month at 10am at the Dingley Village Neighbourhood Centre.

rows.datetime_text: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday
rows.description: We seek to connect people to God and each other. Come join us on Sundays at 10am for our traditional church service, which is also live streamed on YouTube. Our Christmas Carols evening will be on Sunday 22 Dec 2024 at 7.30pm and our Christmas Day service will be on Wednesday 25 Dec at 10am. Unleash the Music group is on the 2nd and 4th Thursday nights of each month at 7.30pm. It's a fun musical group for all types of people to play or sing popular music from the past. Bark and Chat Morning Tea for dog owners, dog lovers and their dogs is on the 3rd Saturday at 10am in Jan, Mar, May, July, Sept, with an annual Dog Church service on the 3rd Sunday of Nov at 10am. More information about our church and activities can be found on our website at: https://heathertondingley.ucavictas.org.au/

rows.name: Melbourne PC User Group
rows.description: Melbourne PC User Group (MelbPC) is a volunteer run not-for-profit association that has run successfully for over 40 years. Who? We’re an inclusive community of learners, makers and sharers who enjoy a wide cross-section of technology, STEAM and creative interests, in both the physical and digital realms. Why? It is affordable, accessible, welcoming and fun with benefits available via a mix of in-person, hybrid and dedicated online resources, projects and events. Where? Our main hub is in Moorabbin (opp. Bunnings), with connected groups based in Melbourne’s Northern and Eastern suburbs, and Sunbury. Our clubrooms are amazing! Our motto is, Members Helping Members! Before visiting us, call (03) 9276 4000 or check our Event Calendar

rows.name: Mentone Probus Club
rows.address: Mentone Life Saving Club, Beach Road, Mentone 3194
rows.description: Mentone Probus Club is about all about fun, friendship and fellowship in our local community. We meet on the third Tuesday of every month at 10am (followed by a catered lunch at 12 noon), at the beautiful Mentone Lifesaving Club. We’re a newly established Probus Club (started in March 2025), now with over 100 members from around bayside (male, female and couples, mainly in our 60’s and 70’s), who enjoy socialising, getting out and about, and having a few laughs. Unfortunately, our club is full at the moment so we're currently placing prospective new members on a waiting list. If you’d like to know more about our club or join our waiting list please get in touch via email at enquiries@mentoneprobus.org.au or visit our website at http://www.mentoneprobus.org.au.

rows.name: Moorabbin Air Museum
rows.description: Formed in 1962, the Museum houses the most complete collection of Australian made aircraft and engines in the world. In addition, the archival collection has become the biggest in the Southern Hemisphere. Run by volunteers and with a growing member base, the Museum is a go to point in the area for group visits, clubs, schools and more. Events are held regularly during the year and there are options to have functions in a hangar or one of the larger aircraft.

rows.name: Moorabbin Rugby Union Football Club
rows.description: We acknowledge our heritage and the proud history of our Club, established in 1965 by a community connected by a common purpose to play the great game and achieve great things. Thanks to this firm groundwork, The Moorabbin Rugby Club has since grown and developed into the Club it is today. LEGACY Our legacy includes 15 First Grade Premierships and the Club has produced representatives playing in Super Rugby, the Rugby World Cup and in Professional Rugby Clubs all round the world. We draw strength and inspiration from this proud history, to continue to work hard so that we build on this legacy and continue to inspire future generations. Without a doubt our ethos remains unchanged - we are our people, a diverse group of individuals, brought together to enjoy and celebrate the opportunity to play this great game. FACILITIES The Club has the good fortune of dedicated rugby facilities with excellent playing fields, modern clubrooms and gym facilities - the only year round rugby facility in Kingston City and the surrounding Bayside, Frankston and Casey areas.  This allows our Club the opportunity for year round rugby and training activities which include Touch Rugby and Sevens Rugby in the off season. COMMUNITY One of the special things about our club is the sense of belonging to a close-knit community. Our people is what makes our club special. We are a diverse and multi-cultural community, united with a common purpose to do good for each other, to work hard, play hard and enjoy this amazing rugby journey. The commitment to be a positive source of energy and to provide the development opportunities to grow the game, is upheld across the Club leadership team from our coaches, key players, committee, and the management team. NEW PLAYERS WELCOME Moorabbin provides the perfect opportunity for players to maximize their potential and transition from community sport to the elite game, while enjoying an exciting brand of rugby within a fantastic community. If you're new to Melbourne, the Club has an extensive network of players, coaches, an active volunteer base, and passionate supporters that will help you get on your feet if you are new to Victoria or Australia.

rows.name: Mordialloc & District Historical Society
rows.description: For 60 years our Society has collected, preserved and displayed thousands of important items of local history, ie: relevant to Mordialloc, Parkdale and Mentone. We operate Kingston's only historical museum which is located behind the Mentone shops and is open to the public on Sundays from 11am - 3pm.

rows.name: Mordialloc Men's Shed
rows.description: Mordialloc Men's Shed is a friendly and welcoming gathering place open to all men regardless of interests, age or background.  New members always welcome! We are a small, social shed.  Come along and make new friends, engage in conversation, enjoy good coffee and a biscuit, play pool or cards, venture into the workshop to work on your own or community projects, partake in occasional excursions. We are located at 1 McDonald Street, Mordialloc , right next the railway line on the Nepean Hwy side, just 200 metres from Mordialloc Station. We are open on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday mornings from 9:00 am to 12:00 noon. You are most welcome to come and visit at any time to see if we are what you are looking for or contact us on 0421 151 284.

rows.name: Probus Club of Dingley Central
rows.location: Salvation Army Kingston Gardens Community Church
rows.description: If you are retired, whether you are male or female, you are invited to come along as a visitor to the Probus Club of Dingley Central on the first Monday of the month at 10 a.m. to see why this Probus Club is so popular. You will be entertained by guest speakers and listen to shared stories. You can also join a coffee/chat group, visit local cafés or go for lunch with like-minded people. You can join the craft group, connect with passionate card players or display your photographic skills. Trips and outings are also very popular. Probus is non-political, non-sectarian and non-profit. The major difference between Probus and many other community clubs is that Probus focuses on friendship, not fundraising. We aim to enrich members’ lives through social connection, engaging activities and shared experiences.

rows.name: Rotary Club of Mordialloc Mentone
rows.description: The Rotary Club of Mordialloc Mentone is active in the local community of Mordialloc, Parkdale & Mentone,  fundraising to support charitable organisations, and partnering with organisations such as the Mordialloc Neighbourhood House, Men's Shed, Salvation Army at Dingley, Fight Parkinson's support group and providing sponsorship for school students to attend Rotary programs. We run a market at the old Mentone Heritage Railway station once a month and put on an annual Gnome & Fairy Festival in March. Heart History Health Walks and a Chatty Cafe at Just Italy in Mentone are some of the many activities supported by the Club. These local projects stand alongside a number of international programs, disaster aid, as well as bushfire and flood relief. Interested in joining? You are welcome to come along to a meeting, most Tuesdays at the Mentone RSL, 6.30pm.

We run a market at the old Mentone Heritage Railway station once a month and put on an annual Gnome & Fairy Festival in March. Heart History Health Walks and a Chatty Cafe at Just Italy in Mentone are some of the many activities supported by the Club. These local projects stand alongside a number of international programs, disaster aid, as well as bushfire and flood relief. Interested in joining? You are welcome to come along to a meeting, most Tuesdays at the Mentone RSL, 6.30pm.

rows.name: Rotary Club of Oakleigh Clayton Huntingdale
rows.description: The Rotary Club of Oakleigh Clayton Huntingdale Inc formed in 2019 when the Rotary clubs of Oakleigh, Clayton and Huntingdale merged to create a new and stronger Club within the cities of Monash and Kingston. With over 160 combined years of service and experience, the Club, Rotary OCH, is definitely well placed to continue the good work of Rotary and to make your community a better place to live. Rotary OCH brings together a team of men and women who meet weekly on Monday evenings from 6.30pm at 319 Clayton Road, Clayton. As a part of Rotary OCH, members and guests enjoy friendship, community service, networking, social activity and personal development through participation in local and international projects. And always doing it with fun. The main fundraiser of Rotary OCH is the Oakleigh Rotary Sunday Market which started more than 30 years ago, and has evolved into a thriving and well-loved local event that brings the community together every Sunday morning. Through its fund-raising efforts Rotary OCH supports local and international communities such as

rows.name: Senior Citizens of the Freccia Azzurra Club Inc.
rows.description: We're a senior citizens group that meet every Tuesday from 9:30am to 4:30pm to socialise with friends and have a good time at the cost of $20 for a 3 course meal for both members and non-members. There is also the option to stay for dinner on a Tuesday and order from our à la carte menu. We partake in several activities such as Bocce, Bingo, Italian Card Games and Table Tennis, as well as occasionally taking day trips. On the last Tuesday of the month from 12:00pm to 4:30pm we have a formal lunch and dance with an Italian band and a 3 course meal at $35 for members of our group, and $40 for non-members. Stay tuned to our Facebook page for all other events that we organise.

rows.name: St Matthew's Anglican Church, Cheltenham
rows.address: Cnr Nepean Highway and Park Road, Cheltenham 3192
rows.description: St Matthew's Anglican church has been a centre of worship in Cheltenham for over 150 years. We experience God’s hospitality through meeting together, praying for each other and for God’s world, and sharing in rituals that help to strengthen our spiritual lives.  Our worship style is traditional Anglican (Anglo-Catholic) with music and children's ministry a regular feature. God's love does not discriminate, and our church is a welcoming and inclusive place for all people. We offer regular services on Sunday at 9.30am and Wednesday at 9.45am, as well as celebrations to mark special days in the Christian calendar. Members of the community also have the opportunity to mark life events such as baptisms, weddings and funerals.  Our beautiful mid-century church is in the heart of Cheltenham, on the corner of Park Road and Nepean Highway. We operate Cheltenham Opportunity Shop in the building next to our church at 161 Park Road Cheltenham, and other spaces within our church buildings are available for use by community organisations, including Matt's Place community meals program, which operates from our Church hall on Thursdays.

rows.name: St Nicholas Anglican Church Mordialloc
rows.description: We meet every Sunday at 9:15am for Holy Communion . Please join us after the service for morning tea fellowship. Things we do: Messy Church: an all-age, informal and fun way of doing Church that is particularly suited to families with children, but all are welcome,  is held on the fourth Sunday of the month except December - ( when there is a special "Messy Christmas Eve" at 5pm, and January when Messy is in recess) from 4.00 - 6.00 pm. Walk Pray Eat: on the 4th Saturday each Month, is a quiet reflective walk, finishing at various cafes for Breakfast, coffee/tea, or just a catchup and fellowship. Mordialloc Pantry: trade your donation for something that can be of use to you. We could also organise a volunteer to collect your items if travelling isn't an option or life is too hectic. The Pantry Cabinet is accessible 24 hours a day. Bible Studies: Wednesday night at 8pm "In Person" bible study on the 2nd and 4th of each month. Please email us or visit our website for further information. ZOOM bible study is on 2nd and 4th Thursdays at 7.30pm. Pastoral Ministries: to the aged and unwell, Spiritual Direction, Weddings, Baptisms, and Funerals conducted by the Vicar and Pastoral Ministry Team.

Things we do: Messy Church: an all-age, informal and fun way of doing Church that is particularly suited to families with children, but all are welcome,  is held on the fourth Sunday of the month except December - ( when there is a special "Messy Christmas Eve" at 5pm, and January when Messy is in recess) from 4.00 - 6.00 pm. Walk Pray Eat: on the 4th Saturday each Month, is a quiet reflective walk, finishing at various cafes for Breakfast, coffee/tea, or just a catchup and fellowship. Mordialloc Pantry: trade your donation for something that can be of use to you. We could also organise a volunteer to collect your items if travelling isn't an option or life is too hectic. The Pantry Cabinet is accessible 24 hours a day. Bible Studies: Wednesday night at 8pm "In Person" bible study on the 2nd and 4th of each month. Please email us or visit our website for further information. ZOOM bible study is on 2nd and 4th Thursdays at 7.30pm. Pastoral Ministries: to the aged and unwell, Spiritual Direction, Weddings, Baptisms, and Funerals conducted by the Vicar and Pastoral Ministry Team.

rows.name: When No One's Watching (WNOW) - Mentone Sunrise Club
rows.description: WNOW creates environments where men feel safe to connect authentically, share openly and learn from their peers to enable them to be happier when they are by themselves and with their loved ones. We want to shake the perceived cultural expectations that are upon the modern man. We are saying it is ok to celebrate emotional vulnerability and be a good man. Its ok to grow and change out of your culturally accepted norm to be a better person for yourself and for the world around us. How do we do this? Sunrise Clubs, where we meet to do a simple workout / mindful movement, share stories, have a dip in the ocean, and most importantly have a coffee and connect with one another. We create a safe, non-judgmental environment where everyone is welcome regardless. Every Wednesday. 6AM. Rain Hail or Shine. Next to Mentone LSC. WNOW is a ACNC registered charity with DGR status ( https://www.acnc.gov.au/charity/charities/dcfb107e-8724-ef11-840b-00224893bffb/profile )

rows.name: Heatherton Dingley Uniting Church
rows.datetime_text: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday
rows.description: We seek to connect people to God and each other. Come join us on Sundays at 10am for our traditional church service, which is also live streamed on YouTube. Our Christmas Carols evening will be on Sunday 22 Dec 2024 at 7.30pm and our Christmas Day service will be on Wednesday 25 Dec at 10am. Unleash the Music group is on the 2nd and 4th Thursday nights of each month at 7.30pm. It's a fun musical group for all types of people to play or sing popular music from the past. Bark and Chat Morning Tea for dog owners, dog lovers and their dogs is on the 3rd Saturday at 10am in Jan, Mar, May, July, Sept, with an annual Dog Church service on the 3rd Sunday of Nov at 10am. More information about our church and activities can be found on our website at: https://heathertondingley.ucavictas.org.au/
rows.recurrence: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday

rows.name: Melbourne 69ers Ten Pin Bowling League
rows.description: We are looking for people of all identities, all abilities, all skill levels. Come for the friendly competition, stay for the community. You might even take home a trophy in our ten-pin bowling league. "Come and Try" a session for just $11.00. ($35.00 per a week after that). Once you meet the league, you won’t want to leave. Location: Zone Bowling Clayton Time: Thursdays, 7:45 PM Got questions? We’ve got answers. Contact Ryan (Text preferred or call) 0409020109 email us melb69rs@hotmail.com

rows.name: Mordialloc Men's Shed
rows.description: Mordialloc Men's Shed is a friendly and welcoming gathering place open to all men regardless of interests, age or background.  New members always welcome! We are a small, social shed.  Come along and make new friends, engage in conversation, enjoy good coffee and a biscuit, play pool or cards, venture into the workshop to work on your own or community projects, partake in occasional excursions. We are located at 1 McDonald Street, Mordialloc , right next the railway line on the Nepean Hwy side, just 200 metres from Mordialloc Station. We are open on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday mornings from 9:00 am to 12:00 noon. You are most welcome to come and visit at any time to see if we are what you are looking for or contact us on 0421 151 284.

rows.name: 'Hand me down' by Andrew Duong
rows.datetime_text:
Next date: Wednesday, 07 October 2026 | 11:00 AM 
	to 04:00 PM
rows.description: Exhibiting a series of paintings exploring inherited items and their cultural significance through an Australian-Cambodian-Chinese lens. Paintings reference stories of second-generation migrants and people born in the 90's, through a playful tone that speaks to values of sharing, appreciation and family.

rows.name: 'Rendered Other and Cast Out' by Elizabeth Cole
rows.datetime_text:
Next date: Wednesday, 07 October 2026 | 11:00 AM 
	to 04:00 PM
rows.description: A multi-disciplinary exhibition that reworks Antarctic and personal archival materials to warn of our uncertain future due to human-caused global warming. The five-part installation references the historic age of polar exploration, colonial-era whaling and the possible post-human consequences of inaction.

rows.name: Stitch with Sappho: Community Textile Installation by Juliet D Collins

rows.description: A collaborative textile and mixed media installation created with community participants; weaving together stitched fragments to reimagine Ancient Greek poet Sappho’s legacy and enduring presence through collective making.

rows.name: Heatherton Dingley Uniting Church
rows.datetime_text: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday
rows.description: We seek to connect people to God and each other. Come join us on Sundays at 10am for our traditional church service, which is also live streamed on YouTube. Our Christmas Carols evening will be on Sunday 22 Dec 2024 at 7.30pm and our Christmas Day service will be on Wednesday 25 Dec at 10am. Unleash the Music group is on the 2nd and 4th Thursday nights of each month at 7.30pm. It's a fun musical group for all types of people to play or sing popular music from the past. Bark and Chat Morning Tea for dog owners, dog lovers and their dogs is on the 3rd Saturday at 10am in Jan, Mar, May, July, Sept, with an annual Dog Church service on the 3rd Sunday of Nov at 10am. More information about our church and activities can be found on our website at: https://heathertondingley.ucavictas.org.au/
rows.recurrence: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday

rows.name: Aspendale Presbyterian Church
rows.description: Aspendale Presbyterian Church is proud to be a local church. We love Jesus, love our community, love the Bible and love visitors. Our Sunday services are at 10am. We are a community of Christians who meet in Aspendale each week. We meet to hear God's truth from the Bible, encourage and support each other, and to practically live out the difference Jesus makes. As a Presbyterian church the church is lead by local elders. The Presbyterian Church originated in Scotland but welcomes all people today. Our Activities Each week we have a Sunday service at 10am with Kids Sunday School where all are welcome.  We also run bible studies, Kids clubs, playgroups, youth group, community events, prayer meetings and community meals.

rows.name: Austin 7 Club Inc Reg No A0003290N
rows.description: We are a one make Vintage Car club and provide sporting and social events, displays and runs for our members. We support the restoration and have activities for owners and supporters of all models of Austin 7 cars that were built from 1923 to 1938 by obtaining parts and technical help to keep the marque alive. Based in Cheltenham. We have 400+ members of all ages. It has always been a family club. Ladies and children are very welcome. The majority of members are in Victoria and many others from interstate with a few international members. We support all models of Austin 7's and encourage the younger members in learning the traditional skills in maintaining these older motor vehicles and their learning their history. The club runs rallies around Victoria and also join in with interstate clubs for other runs. The club has Full, Family and also Associate membership's if you don't own an Austin 7. All welcome. Our Monthly General Meeting is on the 1st Wednesday of the month except January. Meetings at 8pm The rooms open from 7:30pm for nibble & natter. The Saturday following the MGM at Noon-2:30 we open up Spare Parts & nibble & natter until 2:30 pm. And on the 3rd Wednesday 7:30-9pm for Spare parts, social chat with tea and coffee. See website www.austin7club.org.

Our rides are organised and conducted with most rides ideally suited to the novice and average cyclist with the emphasis of supporting and encouraging new members. We are not a competitive club and we welcome all riders. Our rides always have one thing in common: people enjoying cycling. Come and join us for healthy outdoors exercise with the companionship and security of a group. Meet new and interesting people with a common interest in cycling. Our rides program is compiled on a rolling three-month basis so there are always three months of planned rides to look forward to. rows.name: Probus Club of Dingley Central
rows.location: Salvation Army Kingston Gardens Community Church
rows.description: If you are retired, whether you are male or female, you are invited to come along as a visitor to the Probus Club of Dingley Central on the first Monday of the month at 10 a.m. to see why this Probus Club is so popular. You will be entertained by guest speakers and listen to shared stories. You can also join a coffee/chat group, visit local cafés or go for lunch with like-minded people. You can join the craft group, connect with passionate card players or display your photographic skills. Trips and outings are also very popular. Probus is non-political, non-sectarian and non-profit. The major difference between Probus and many other community clubs is that Probus focuses on friendship, not fundraising. We aim to enrich members’ lives through social connection, engaging activities and shared experiences.

rows.name: Rotary Club of Mordialloc Mentone
rows.description: The Rotary Club of Mordialloc Mentone is active in the local community of Mordialloc, Parkdale & Mentone,  fundraising to support charitable organisations, and partnering with organisations such as the Mordialloc Neighbourhood House, Men's Shed, Salvation Army at Dingley, Fight Parkinson's support group and providing sponsorship for school students to attend Rotary programs. We run a market at the old Mentone Heritage Railway station once a month and put on an annual Gnome & Fairy Festival in March. Heart History Health Walks and a Chatty Cafe at Just Italy in Mentone are some of the many activities supported by the Club. These local projects stand alongside a number of international programs, disaster aid, as well as bushfire and flood relief. Interested in joining? You are welcome to come along to a meeting, most Tuesdays at the Mentone RSL, 6.30pm.

rows.name: Rotary Club of Oakleigh Clayton Huntingdale
rows.description: The Rotary Club of Oakleigh Clayton Huntingdale Inc formed in 2019 when the Rotary clubs of Oakleigh, Clayton and Huntingdale merged to create a new and stronger Club within the cities of Monash and Kingston. With over 160 combined years of service and experience, the Club, Rotary OCH, is definitely well placed to continue the good work of Rotary and to make your community a better place to live. Rotary OCH brings together a team of men and women who meet weekly on Monday evenings from 6.30pm at 319 Clayton Road, Clayton. As a part of Rotary OCH, members and guests enjoy friendship, community service, networking, social activity and personal development through participation in local and international projects. And always doing it with fun. The main fundraiser of Rotary OCH is the Oakleigh Rotary Sunday Market which started more than 30 years ago, and has evolved into a thriving and well-loved local event that brings the community together every Sunday morning. rows.name: St Matthew's Anglican Church, Cheltenham
rows.address: Cnr Nepean Highway and Park Road, Cheltenham 3192
rows.description: St Matthew's Anglican church has been a centre of worship in Cheltenham for over 150 years. We experience God’s hospitality through meeting together, praying for each other and for God’s world, and sharing in rituals that help to strengthen our spiritual lives.  Our worship style is traditional Anglican (Anglo-Catholic) with music and children's ministry a regular feature. God's love does not discriminate, and our church is a welcoming and inclusive place for all people. We offer regular services on Sunday at 9.30am and Wednesday at 9.45am, as well as celebrations to mark special days in the Christian calendar. Members of the community also have the opportunity to mark life events such as baptisms, weddings and funerals.  Our beautiful mid-century church is in the heart of Cheltenham, on the corner of Park Road and Nepean Highway. We operate Cheltenham Opportunity Shop in the building next to our church at 161 Park Road Cheltenham, and other spaces within our church buildings are available for use by community organisations, including Matt's Place community meals program, which operates from our Church hall on Thursdays.

rows.name: When No One's Watching (WNOW) - Mentone Sunrise Club
rows.description: WNOW creates environments where men feel safe to connect authentically, share openly and learn from their peers to enable them to be happier when they are by themselves and with their loved ones. We want to shake the perceived cultural expectations that are upon the modern man. We are saying it is ok to celebrate emotional vulnerability and be a good man. Its ok to grow and change out of your culturally accepted norm to be a better person for yourself and for the world around us. How do we do this? Sunrise Clubs, where we meet to do a simple workout / mindful movement, share stories, have a dip in the ocean, and most importantly have a coffee and connect with one another. We create a safe, non-judgmental environment where everyone is welcome regardless. Every Wednesday. 6AM. Rain Hail or Shine. Next to Mentone LSC. WNOW is a ACNC registered charity with DGR status ( https://www.acnc.gov.au/charity/charities/dcfb107e-8724-ef11-840b-00224893bffb/profile )
